method: blind review of untouched repos (holdout + random sample): every in-scope edge judged by scripted census of wrong patterns, validated by hand; per-repo precision, the target met when the worst repo reaches it; pooled edge-weighted per language alongside

known_gaps: X-macros defined by the including file are not expanded (behaviour not yet decided in SPEC)
operator() on typed objects is reported as a callback
function-local typedefs and namespace-member calls (DirectX::XM…) are under-resolved
some namespace-qualified free-function calls are missed (calls into a nested namespace, ::global calls, an overload calling another)
delegating constructor calls (: Circle(…)) get no edge
calls through a function-pointer parameter written (*op)() get no edge
calls in instance field initializers have the file as caller instead of Type#field, and the implicit <init> edge is missing
a call through a reference parameter to a method declared in a header is missed
calls through a pointer-to-member ((w.*method)()) get no edge
?. calls and target-typed new() are missed
delegate fields and => getters are under-resolved
receivers bound by is-patterns (x is Item matched) stay low
type parameters with a where-bound are named T#m, not the bound
a lambda bound to a local is not a named nested function
calls on a call result whose declared return type is in the scan stay .m low
a nested defmodule alias applies before its defmodule line (aliases are lexical, in source order)
packages that fail to type-check are not graphed (reported in coverage)
range-over-func loop bodies (for x := range seq) get no edges (behaviour not yet decided in SPEC)
methods of some generic types get no edges, and calls into scanned generics are medium
calls in package-level var initializers get no edges
a call through a method value (bark := d.Bark; bark()) is named Dog#Bark medium instead of the callback rule
go.note: precision is high; the gaps are missing edges, not wrong ones

known_gaps: properties declared by getters and typed field chains are left as low recv.m
type parameters with a bound are named T#m, not the bound
a bare call not defined anywhere in the scan is Type#m medium instead of a low guess
enum constant declarations get no Enum#<clinit> → Enum#<init> edge
operator applications are not emitted (behaviour not yet decided in SPEC)

s-orc.ruling: adjudications.md: Round 2026-11-17 s-orc v10: same P1 spec-gap ruling (156-91)

s-newman.ruling: adjudications.md: ## s-newman: 7 _.assign/_.assignIn member edges are a spec gap (25-7)

known_gaps: companion operator invoke and factory functions named like a type are reported as constructors
superclass constructor calls in class headers and infix calls are not emitted; constructor default values get an empty caller
secondary-constructor delegation : this(…) gets no edge
secondary-constructor : super(…) / : this(…) delegation gets no edge
local fun is named Type#f, not Type#m.f; val f = { } is not a named nested function
kotlin.note: files the grammar cannot parse are reported as partial coverage (syntax_error)

known_gaps: typedef aliases of class types are not expanded; @catch parameters are untyped
receivers that are parameterless message results stay .m low

receivers typed id

by a property or ivar stay low
[[T alloc] init] in .mm class methods gives .init low; file-scope macro uses in .m get no edge
a C function call in another .m file is missed
include chains and local module aliases are not followed
class methods (#m) have no caller IDs and no call edges
operators are not emitted (behaviour not yet decided in SPEC)
calls through a record field holding a function (t.on_event x) get no edge
methods from traits resolve to the using class at medium
parent::m() with a parent outside the scan becomes parent.m
receivers that are parameterless method results with a declared return type stay .m low
receivers typed by $x = new T at file top level stay low
PHP first-class callable syntax $this->m(...) is reported as a call
anonymous-class members are named as methods of the enclosing class instead of folding; no constructor edge for new class extends Base
enum-case receivers (Suit::Hearts->color()) stay .m low
callable attributes set by a superclass or tuple assignment are under-resolved
a lambda bound to a local is not a named nested function (callee is a callback, body folds)
.call on a Proc or lambda is a method call, not a callback
methods inside Const = Struct.new do … end blocks get the enclosing class as caller
bare new in class methods is not Type#<init>; recv::Const receivers are glued into the type ID
a call of a top-level def is #name medium instead of the free function
code in a class body has the class as caller instead of the file
receivers bound by match/if-let patterns, turbofish calls and user Deref impls are under-typed
calls through an fn-pointer field ((self.on_click)()) get no edge
enum-variant receivers (Dir::North.flip()) stay .m low
calls written without parentheses are never emitted
symbolic and infix operator calls are never emitted
a bare call of a member inherited from an external base is a low bare name

s-dafny-vscode.ruling: adjudications.md: ## s-dafny-vscode: 4 unannotated for-of loop-variable edges are a spec gap (31-4)

known_gaps: function-valued properties called as this.f() are reported as methods
getters and parameterless methods used as receivers stay low
static calls on instantiated generic types (std.AutoHashMap(K, V).init) are .m low
calls in file-level const initializers and some decl-literal forms (return .init(), .field = .x()) are not emitted
struct { fn g }.g local function aliases are reported as callbacks (behaviour not yet decided in SPEC)
function-local const aliases of functions are callbacks, not their target
receivers typed by an optional capture or file-scope var stay low
calls through function-pointer fields are methods (T#cb) instead of callbacks
